messages.subject: error in user-define functions (to generate restricted cubic spline terms)
parts:
data {
  int<lower=0> N; 
  int<lower=0> y[N];
  int<lower=0, upper=1> Gender[N];
  real<lower=0> backpain[N];
  real Age[N];
  int<lower=0> M;  
  int<lower=0, upper=M> practice[N];
  int<lower=0> Ncut;
} 

functions {
  matrix rcsfun(vector x, real knots[4]) {
    vector x1;
    vector x2;
    vector x3;
    x1 = x;
    x2 = ((x-knots[1] > 0) * ((x-knots[1])^3) - (x-knots[3]>0) * ((x-knots[3])^3) * (knots[4]-knots[1])/(knots[4]-knots[3]) + (x-knots[4]>0) * ((x-knots[4])^3) * (knots[3]-knots[1])/(knots[4]-knots[3]))/((knots[4]-knots[1])^2);
    x3 = (x-knots[2]>0) * ((x-knots[2])^3) - (x-knots[3]>0) * ((x-knots[3])^3) * (knots[4]-knots[2])/(knots[4]-knots[3]) + (x-knots[4]>0) * ((x-knots[4])^3) * (knots[3]-knots[2])/(knots[4]-knots[3])/((knots[4]-knots[1])^2);
  return append_col(x1, x2, x3);
  }
}

generated quantities {
  real Age2[N];
  real Age3[N];
  Age2 = rcsfun(Age, knot.age)[,2];
  Age3 = rcsfun(Age, knot.age)[,3];
}

parameters {
  real beta_backpain;
  real beta_gender;
  real beta_age1;
  real beta_age2;
  real beta_age3;
  real b[M];
  ordered[Ncut] a;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
} 

model {
  for (i in 1:N) {
    y[i] ~ ordered_logistic(beta_gender * Gender[i] + beta_backpain * backpain[i] + beta_age1 * Age[i] + beta_age2 * Age2[i] + beta_age3 * Age3[i] + b[practice[i]], a); 
  }                                                             
  b ~ normal(0, sigma); 
  beta_backpain ~ normal(0, 100); 
  beta_gender ~ normal(0, 100); 
  beta_age1 ~ normal(0, 100); 
  beta_age2 ~ normal(0, 100); 
  beta_age3 ~ normal(0, 100); 
  sigma ~ cauchy(0,5); 
}

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] error in user-define functions (to generate restricted cubic spline terms)
parts:
There are dozens of syntactic problems with this code. The first
three that popped out to me are

1. functions block must come first

2. no . in variable names

3. no sizing in arguments to functions.

That error message we provide isn't super helpful, but it does
point to exactly where your problem is.

- Bob

First, I'd suggest getting acquainted with Stan running simpler
programs so you can learn the syntax.

Then build up complex models a bit at a time.

And read the error messages. It would help to keep your lines
to under 80 characters to do that. I can't figure out where
your current error is, but the error messages says you're supplying
something an index that isn't indexable.
